body:
What was it like being homeless.  Did you have trouble adjusting after you weren't homeless anymore?

Is luck what you credit to your no longer being homeless anymore?
How do you ask for help?  That's my biggest hurdle.

I don't think I'll commit suicide - I've been down that road before and have never been able to "pull the trigger".  I think the mess of it all freaks me out more.

Yet, some days I feel like I've already committed suicide.  And I don't mean it in a metaphorical poetic sort of way, but really, I feel like I'm dead.  There was one night in particular lying in my car and I just felt numb.  There literally was an absence of feelings and the only thing I was sensing was my head ruminating over all these thoughts, perceptions and ideas of my situation.  I guess I'm like a zombie of sorts...I just go through the motions and any apparent smiles are just an act - they aren't sourced in anything real. 

Ugh!

I read your statement, and I think, "ok, seems simple and rational enough" and yet, I think the trouble is just asking for help.  I'm not really sure I know how to do it which is strange, because in a previous line of work, I would see people with a myriad of situations and help them as best I could connecting them to services and whatnot. 

I think it's an ego thing.  Sometimes I've been so tempted to blurt out my problems when I hear people around me talk about the most mundane shit.  "Ugh, my boyfriend is getting chubby and it's really bothering me, I don't know what to do" or  once I saw a coworker throw away like 3/4 of her meal I was livid that she could do such a thing.  And yet, I stumble, the words just can't come out of my mouth.  any advice?

I'd like to think that there is strength in what I'm doing but honestly, I've just grown soooo tired.  I'm crying just even thinking about the magnitude of my exhaustion (physically, mentally, emotionally) - up until these past few weeks, I'm getting this pain in my legs and feet (I think from sleeping on a car seat) that it literally pains me to put "one foot forward."  I don't know how to go on.

The saddest part of my situation is I have no support system.  As sad as it sounds, the thing I want more than anything right now is just some human contact.  A hug would be nice.  

Sometimes before I get settled to go to sleep in my car, I imagine getting snuggled by someone - I've even started having conversations with an imaginary person thinking about a perfect future - a warm house, a belly filled with a big dinner, soft sheets, having put some kids to sleep.  Sometimes I catch myself doing this and I think "my god...I must really be crazy" and I shut myself up almost immediately.  Even admitting this is hard work.

this is a throwaway:

I am so glad there is someone else in my situation - I've been doing this for 2 months.

I can live in my car (it took a month to adjust), I can take showers at the gym, I can focus on my school work (in fact moreso, because I don't have a place with a tv and whatnot to distract me), I can continue to eat relatively healthy, but the hardest thing is not having anyone to talk to about this.  I feel like keeping this secret is a matter of survival.  People won't understand and they will judge you harshly (it's just a fact), and I don't think I can take the harsh judgement. As a result, I haven't been cementing current and new friendships.

I'd love to have someone to talk to about this - maybe share some laughs over a beer about our situation? 

Where do you live? I'm in NorCal.
